title: Common carp aquaculture in Neolithic China dates back 8,000 years
version: Nature Ecology & Evolution 3, pp. 1415–1418 (2019); full publisher text inspected through a mirror.

passages.quote: was present at the Early Neolithic Jiahu site, Henan Province, China, by around 6000 bc

passages.note: Dates the three Jiahu phases; Period III has two modal groups of estimated body lengths. The assemblage has a relatively high proportion of common carp.

Infers a stage of management in marshy waters. The measured remains are not a direct witness of any particular pond or channel; the model draws on comparison with archaeological and recent Japanese specimens.

file.method: Passages of about 500 characters either side of each cited quotation, cut from the fetched page text.
